findings.excerpt:
change eval (fun _ : Unit => (0 : ℚ)) (positiveUnivariate v) = 0
  rw [eval_zero_eq_coefficient, positiveUnivariate_zero]
findings.problem: The canonical zero normal form for evaluating a vector polynomial at zero is not available to `simp`. Both facts used here, `eval (fun _ => 0) p = coefficients p 0` and `coefficients (positiveUnivariate v) 0 = 0`, are stated as plain theorems rather than `@[simp]` lemmas, so this proof has to change the goal and then rewrite with both names explicitly. The same pattern recurs downstream: `NativeCoveredCommonFactorization.lean` lines 22-23 and `NormalizedComparisonOrbit.lean` line 91 list `eval_zero_eq_coefficient` in `simp only`, while `NativeSubspaceFreeModel.lean` line 226 repeats the exact two-step rewrite used here. `VectorPolynomial.eval` is defined through a tensor product, so the existing `[simp]` lemma `eval_tmul` only reduces tensor-factor terms; there is no default simp rule for `eval (fun _ => 0) p` with arbitrary `p`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `[simp]` to the declaration of `Erdos3.VectorPolynomial.eval_zero_eq_coefficient` in `WeightedOrbitNormalization.lean`, and add `[simp]` to `Erdos3.VectorPolynomial.positiveUnivariate_zero` in `QuantitativeOuterPolynomialProducts.lean`. With both attributes, `eval (fun _ => 0) (positiveUnivariate v)` rewrites to `coefficients (positiveUnivariate v) 0` and then to `0`, so the last step of this theorem can use `simpa`/`simp` instead of the explicit `change` and `rw`. No reverse simp rule for either identity was found in the inspected sources, so this does not introduce a rewrite cycle.
findings.benefit: This establishes the desired normal form `eval (fun _ => 0) p` to `coefficients p 0`, and `coefficients (positiveUnivariate v) 0` to `0`, once for all users. It removes repeated `simp only` lists and explicit two-step rewrites in the native and polynomial-orbit developments, and makes goals produced by `polynomialOrbitEval_coord` simplify uniformly without unfolding `VectorPolynomial.eval` or relying on tensor-factor lemmas.

    intro d

findings.problem: The proof must unfold the definition `monomialScale` and then use the non-simp Finsupp lemma `Finsupp.prod_single_index` merely to evaluate `monomialScale` at a single-index exponent. The hypothesis of `positiveUnivariate_coefficientBound` is stated with `monomialScale T (Finsupp.single () (d.val + 1))`, so callers are forced into this definitional expansion. The identical `simpa only [monomialScale, Finsupp.prod_single_index, pow_zero]` appears in `SharedFreeAffineOrbitFamily.lean` line 520, and `PolynomialKernelDirectionBudget.lean` lines 35-36 separately re-derive the single-index case as `monomialScale T (Finsupp.single i 1) = T i`. `monomialScale` currently has only `monomialScale_zero` as a simp lemma, so there is no canonical rule for `monomialScale T (Finsupp.single i n)`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a canonical single-index lemma next to `monomialScale` in `VectorPolynomialReconstruction.lean`, for example:

```lean
@[simp] theorem monomialScale_single {σ : Type*} (T : σ → ℝ) (i : σ) (n : ℕ) :
    monomialScale T (Finsupp.single i n) = T i ^ n := by
  rw [monomialScale, Finsupp.prod_single_index (by simp)]
```

Then replace line 116 by `simpa only [monomialScale_single] using herr d` (or let default `simp` use the new rule). The `n = 0` case is not a cycle: `Finsupp.single_zero`/`monomialScale_zero` and `monomialScale_single` both reduce to `1`, and the right-hand side contains no `monomialScale`.
findings.benefit: The desired normal form is `monomialScale T (Finsupp.single i n) = T i ^ n`, so users no longer unfold `monomialScale` or depend on the internals of `Finsupp.prod`. This directly discharges the bound hypothesis in this theorem and the same pattern in the shared-free-affine family, and it turns the separately re-derived single-index identity in `PolynomialKernelDirectionBudget` into an instance of a general simp lemma.
